digest.component_or_area: Pandoc verification and corpus replay infrastructure
propositions: Gerrit Verify performs complete live-Pandoc corpus work contributing a measured 184.32-second macOS lower bound overhead that should be eliminated from the per-change hot path.

The implementation must retain all behavioral, contractual, and platform assertions while replacing broad corpus subprocess replay with committed deterministic Pandoc outputs consumed by a static fail-closed converter.

Three representative live product-path bodies (one each from code_arrow, table, prose strata) and compact version/platform/argv/stdin/timeout probes must remain in routine Verify to preserve external contract coverage.

A new pandoc-corpus-replay external workflow job must execute the complete corpus (178 bodies, 1,383 ordered real conversions) through actual Pandoc on ubuntu-latest and macos-latest on weekly and manual dispatch schedules.
The committed fixture artifacts must be deterministic, below per-file size gates, identify Pandoc 3.6.1 and platform binary SHA-256 values, and include a non-writing validation command.

Paired same-host A/B testing measured a 90.8% wall-time reduction in the focused phase (42s to 4s) when broad corpus assertions consumed static outputs, proving subprocess replay was the removable cost.
